results.quote: Fix a compact interval U\subset(0,1). There exists a constant C_\mu(U)<\infty such that for every n\ge1 and every s\ge K-1, if t=n+s, \alpha=n/t, and \alpha\in U, then |\Gamma_{n,s}^{\mathrm{disc}}(\mu)-(t/T_\alpha^\star(\mu)+\log t)|\le C_\mu(U).

There exists an instance-dependent constant C_\mu<\infty such that for every \eta\in(0,1) there is an event \mathcal{G}_\eta with \mathbb{P}_\mu(\mathcal{G}_\eta)\ge1-\eta and, on \mathcal{G}_\eta, simultaneously for all t\ge K and all pairs i\neq j, |V_t(i,j)-V_t^\mu(i,j)|\le C_\mu\left(\sqrt{N_{\mathrm{eff},t}(i,j)H_t(\eta)}+H_t(\eta)\right).

Fix \beta\in(0,1) and a compact interval U\subset(0,1) containing \beta in its interior. Let t_U be an almost-surely finite U-stabilization time. Then there exist instance-dependent constants C_{\mu,0}(U), C_{\mu,1}(U), C_{\mu,2}(U), C_{\mu,3}(U)<\infty such that, for every \delta\in(0,1/2] and every \eta\in(0,1/4], with probability at least 1-3\eta, \tau_\delta\le(1+C_{\mu,0}(U))t_U+T_\beta^\star(\mu)\log(1/\delta)+C_{\mu,1}(U)\sqrt{\log(1/\delta)(\log(K/\eta)+\log\log(e/\delta))}+C_{\mu,2}(U)(\log(K/\eta)+\log\log(e/\delta))+C_{\mu,3}(U).

Fix a compact interval U\subset(0,1) containing \beta in its interior. Under the standing unique-best-arm assumption, the unguarded algorithm admits instance-dependent constants A_{\mu,\beta,U}, B_{\mu,\beta,U}, D_{\mu,\beta,U}>0 such that for every \delta\in(0,1/2] and \eta\in(0,1/4], \mathbb{P}_\mu\big(\tau_\delta\le T_\beta^\star(\mu)\log(1/\delta)+A_{\mu,\beta,U}\sqrt{\log(1/\delta)(\log(K/\eta)+\log\log(e/\delta))}+B_{\mu,\beta,U}(\log(K/\eta)+\log\log(e/\delta))+D_{\mu,\beta,U}\eta^{-a_\mu}(\log(e/\eta))^{b_\mu}\big)\ge 1-4\eta.

results.problem: Bernoulli β-EB-TCI best-arm identification (unguarded, with finite-mean sufficient exploration)
results.quote: Consider the unguarded algorithm and fix a compact interval U\subset(0,1) containing \beta in its interior. Assume finite-mean sufficient exploration: there exist a constant c_\mathrm{se}>0 and an almost-surely finite random time T_\mathrm{se} with \mathbb{E}_\mu[T_\mathrm{se}]<\infty such that \min_{i\in[K]}N_{t,i}\ge c_\mathrm{se}\sqrt{t/K}\forall t\ge T_\mathrm{se}. Then there exists a U-stabilization time t_U that admits a summable upper-quantile bound. Consequently, there are instance-dependent constants C_{\mu,1}, C_{\mu,2}, C_{\mu,3}<\infty such that, for all \delta\in(0,1/2], \mathbb{E}_\mu[\tau_\delta]\le T_\beta^\star(\mu)\log(1/\delta)+C_{\mu,1}\sqrt{\log(1/\delta)\log\log(e/\delta)}+C_{\mu,2}\log\log(e/\delta)+C_{\mu,3}.

results.problem: Bernoulli β-EB-TCI best-arm identification (unguarded, pairwise-distinct means, tie-breaking variant of Jourdan et al. [9])
results.quote: Assume that all arm means are pairwise distinct. Consider the unguarded Bernoulli \beta-EB-TCI variant with the same empirical-best leader and transportation-cost challenger indices as Algorithm 1, but with a tie-breaking convention covered by Jourdan et al. [9], in particular their uniform tie-breaking convention. Then there exist instance-dependent constants C_{\mu,1}, C_{\mu,2}, C_{\mu,3}<\infty such that, for all \delta\in(0,1/2], \mathbb{E}_\mu[\tau_\delta]\le T_\beta^\star(\mu)\log(1/\delta)+C_{\mu,1}\sqrt{\log(1/\delta)\log\log(e/\delta)}+C_{\mu,2}\log\log(e/\delta)+C_{\mu,3}.

Assume the exploration guard in Algorithm 1 is enabled. Then for all t\ge K, \min_{i\in[K]}N_{t,i}\ge\left\lfloor\sqrt{t/K}\right\rfloor-1. Consequently, for every \eta\in(0,1), t_\mathrm{sep}(\eta)\le K(n_\star(\eta)+1)^2, and, for every compact interval U\subset(0,1) containing \beta in its interior, there exists a U-stabilization time t_U whose high-probability upper bound is polynomial in \log(1/\eta).

Assume the exploration guard in Algorithm 1 is enabled and let \mu be any Bernoulli instance with a unique best arm. Then there exist instance-dependent constants C_{\mu,1}, C_{\mu,2}, C_{\mu,3}>0 such that, for all \delta\in(0,1/2], \mathbb{E}_\mu[\tau_\delta]\le T_\beta^\star(\mu)\log(1/\delta)+C_{\mu,1}\sqrt{\log(1/\delta)\log\log(e/\delta)}+C_{\mu,2}\log\log(e/\delta)+C_{\mu,3}.
